summary: Tested the new admin error-events feed, the issues admin endpoints, the /admin-issues operator screen on web at 390x844, and the Guardian public page with details mode on, using the public preview URL. Backend: 11/11 tests pass. Error-events: no key, a wrong key and a user JWT all get 401. Response shape is {items,count,total,by_route,by_error_type}, the route and error_type filters work, created_at is an ISO string, there is no _id, and items carry only the allowed fields. Guardian page: a real journey shows name, destination and times with no coordinates, area, accuracy or map/Leaflet/tile references, even after a location push (28.61/77.20, 'Connaught Place'). After mark-safe it shows 'Arrived safely' and still has no location. A random token gets 200 'Link not found' with no journey data. Frontend: every requested flow works — a wrong key shows 'Invalid admin key.' and stays locked; the right key unlocks; tapping a row expands the full description; the status pill goes New -> In progress (kept after Refresh) -> Resolved; the New / In progress / Resolved filters refetch and list only matching reports; the Server errors tab loads, shows route chips and route filtering works. One privacy question: a journey whose sharing was turned off still shows name and destination. There are a few small UI issues. No deprecated Expo packages in the reviewed file.

minor.issue: When the owner has turned sharing off (sharing_revoked_at set), details mode still shows the traveller name, destination, start time and check-in time under a 'Sharing turned off' banner. Turning sharing off should probably stop showing even these details (e.g. send the neutral or private page). This needs a product decision. No location leaks either way.

_fmt_dt shows times as stored (UTC) with no time-zone label, e.g. '07:30 PM' for a journey started at 01:00 IST. A guardian in India would misread the start and check-in times. Convert to IST or add a 'UTC' label.

The _status_html page includes <meta name=referrer content=strict-origin>, which loosens the no-referrer response header. Only the origin leaks, not the token path, so the risk is low, but the two are inconsistent.

by_route and by_error_type are counted from the limited items list (at most 200), while total uses count_documents. With more than 200 events the chip counts will be lower than the real numbers. Use an aggregation instead.

ui_bugs.issue: Shows 'Server errors (0)' before the tab has been opened, because the errors are not loaded yet. It looks like there are no errors when there may be some.
The count is the length of the current filtered list (e.g. 'Reports (0)' under the In progress filter), not the total.
Advancing a status under an active filter (e.g. New) changes the row in place, so a row that no longer matches stays in the filtered list until Refresh.

issues: The floating red 'Help' (Report a problem) button sits on top of the operator screen and can cover rows and the trace text at the bottom-right. Consider hiding it on /admin-issues.
The 'All' status chip, the category chips and the route chips have no testID.
Chips and the status pill are 36px tall, under the 44px minimum touch target. Acceptable for a web-only operator tool, but noted.

action_items: Product decision: should the Guardian details page for a journey whose sharing was turned off (sharing_revoked_at) still show name and destination? If not, send _not_found_html or _private_html for revoked journeys in _details_html_for.
Guardian page timestamps: convert to IST or show the time zone in _fmt_dt.
Admin UI: hide or omit the error count on the Server errors tab until errors have loaded (or fetch both feeds on unlock). Optionally show total counts on the tabs.
Optional: hide the floating Help button on /admin-issues, add testIDs to the All / category / route chips, and compute by_route / by_error_type with an aggregation.
critical_code_review_comments: admin-issues.tsx: the admin key is held only in component state (not persisted). Good.
The details page escapes name and destination (&, <, >). Values appear only in text and <title> context, so quotes are not exploitable there.
The token is not echoed in the details HTML (verified).
seed_data_creation: Temporary data only, each piece deleted by its own id or token afterwards: one TEST_it97 issue report, one synthetic error_events doc (route /api/__TEST_it97_ui__), and journeys owned by voicetest2026. A real tester report ('Unable to send message') was left untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The ADMIN_KEY can be read from /app/backend/.env inside the playwright script, so it never has to be printed. The error_events collection was empty in preview, so seed a synthetic doc (see _it97_ui_seed.py) to exercise route chips. Issue reports are rate limited to 20 per user per hour. The preview DB holds real tester reports: only change the status of your own TEST_ reports.
